question: Why did Emma, a top girls' name in 1880s America, become the most popular again in the 2000s?
answer: Because a name sounds old only while old people carry it. By the 1970s Emma had sunk far down the list, attached to grandmothers; once that generation thinned out, it sounded fresh to parents who had never met an Emma their own age. In 2008 it topped the US list.
move: A style looks dated while people you know still wear it.
ask: Which old habit or idea have I dismissed only because it reminds me of the people who had it?
source: US Social Security Administration, Popular Baby Names
